newsitem.title: USA: Dun&Bradstreet seeks 7 pct EPS growth in 97.
newsitem.headline: Dun&Bradstreet seeks 7 pct EPS growth in 97.

text.p: Dun & Bradstreet Corp said Wednesday that its goal will continue to be to increase earnings at a rate of between five percent and seven percent for 1997 over 1996.
In the first quarter ended March 31, the company said earnings grew by 22 percent from the year-earlier period, adjusted for discontinued operations and extraordinary charges.
The company said it was encouraged with its performance during the quarter, but noted that the first quarter is the least significant of the year in terms of earnings.
The company said that on an 'as adjusted' basis, earnings for the 1996 first quarter represented only about 11 percent of the year's total profits.

Dun & Bradstreet Corp consists of Dun & Bradstreet, which provides commercial credit and business marketing information; Moody's Investors Service, a debt rating agency and financial publisher; and Reuben H. Donnelley, a marketer of yellow pages advertising in the U.S.
